title: Unlocated is a coverage-qualified terminal classification

memory.durable_rule: A historical artifact may be classified as unlocated only after a retained coverage envelope demonstrates exhaustive traversal of all accessible refs, reachable commits, historical paths, and deleted-path evidence with no known blind spots. Search silence, default-branch absence, indexed-code absence, or failure to retrieve a candidate are bounded negative observations and must not be promoted to unlocated or absent.
observed: M-004, M-005, and M-006 remain unresolved in the canonical continuity queue.

The immutable-origin candidate contract requires refs_enumerated, reachable_commits_traversed, historical_paths_checked, deleted_paths_checked, and an empty known_blind_spots list before verified origin can be accepted.
The available GitHub connector can retrieve known files and search indexed repository content, but this run did not produce a retained exhaustive ref and commit traversal.
inferred: A negative lookup result is meaningful only within the declared retrieval method and scope.
The classification unlocated is stronger than no candidate found because it asserts coverage completeness.
Origin verification and unlocated classification are dual terminal outcomes of the same exhaustive coverage process.
proposed: Represent each M-004 through M-006 resolution attempt with one coverage envelope and one outcome enum: verified_origin, unlocated_after_exhaustive_coverage, unresolved_incomplete_coverage, or conflicting_candidates.

Require retained raw ref inventory, traversal method, commit count, path-history results, deleted-path checks, retrieval timestamps, and explicit blind spots before permitting unlocated_after_exhaustive_coverage.
superseded: No indexed result means the artifact never existed.
Default-branch absence is equivalent to repository-history absence.
Repeated failed searches eventually become exhaustive by accumulation without a declared coverage model.
unresolved: Exhaustive accessible ref inventory for the repository.
Reachable commit traversal and historical/deleted path search for M-004, M-005, and M-006.
Immutable assignment objects or an evidence-backed unlocated classification for each identifier.

contradiction_resolution.apparent_conflict: The team has multiple negative searches but cannot call the artifacts unlocated.
contradiction_resolution.resolution: The searches are valid bounded observations, while unlocated is a terminal coverage claim. They operate at different evidentiary levels and are not contradictory.

falsification_route: Produce a retained exhaustive traversal showing that the stated coverage dimensions were not necessary to classify an artifact as unlocated without increasing false absence claims.
Locate an accepted governance rule that explicitly permits unlocated classification from bounded indexed search alone.
